recent.question: Bari: Completed Match: Massimo Giunta vs Federico Arnaboldi
recent.what_happened: Giunta and Arnaboldi played their first-round Bari Challenger match on 29 September 2026 as scheduled. It went to a normal finish with no retirement or walkover, so the market resolved Yes.
recent.what_we_missed: Most ATP Challenger matches finish normally, about 93–96% of the time. Nothing in our facts pointed to an injury or withdrawal. The researched forecast (0.48) put too much weight on vague worries: Arnaboldi played three qualifying matches, one opponent retired against him, and the ATP page hadn't posted a result yet, even though the match hadn't started. It ended up below both the market (0.71) and the forecast made without research (0.93).
recent.lesson: For 'match completed' markets, start from the roughly 95% completion base rate and only move well below it when there's specific evidence, like a reported injury, a withdrawal, or a player retiring in their previous match. General fatigue or a result not yet posted isn't enough.

suggested_change.change: Block any match-completion forecast below 0.80 unless the research cites a specific injury, withdrawal, or retirement by one of the two players in this event.

recent.question: Bari: Completed Match: Imanol Lopez Morillo vs Martin Krumich
recent.what_happened: The market resolved No, so the Bari Challenger first-round match between Lopez Morillo and Krumich did not finish through normal play. It most likely ended in a retirement or a walkover. I couldn't confirm which from public sources: the Flashscore and TennisTemple pages returned no retrieved score.
recent.what_we_missed: When the forecast was made, before the match, the market priced completion at only 0.54. Challenger matches normally complete about 97% of the time, so a price that low almost certainly meant traders knew something, such as a withdrawal, an injury, or a posted walkover. The research never looked for what that was and relied only on the base rate and a 'no injuries reported' preview. The 0.56 forecast roughly followed the market, but the claude_direct forecast of 0.95 ignored it entirely.
recent.lesson: If a completion market trades far below the roughly 95–97% base rate, assume there is outside information (a withdrawal, an injury, or a lucky-loser swap) and look for it before forecasting above the market.

suggested_change.change: Flag completion markets priced 20+ points below the base rate, and require a targeted search for withdrawals, walkovers, updated order of play, or lucky-loser replacements before any forecast above the market price is allowed.

recent.question: Adana: Completed Match: Polina Iatcenko vs Erika Andreeva
recent.what_happened: The first-round match in Adana between Iatcenko and qualifier Erika Andreeva went ahead on September 29, 2026, around 10:10 UTC, and was played to the end, so the market resolved YES. My searches did not show the score or who won.
recent.what_we_missed: No evidence pointed to a retirement, walkover or cancellation. Main-draw WTA 125 matches finish normally about 93–96% of the time. The researched forecast of 0.49 treated a thin worry (Iatcenko coming straight from the Ankara event the week before) and a strangely low market price of 0.545 as if they were real signs of risk. Neither justified going below about 90%.
recent.lesson: For 'match completed' markets, start from the roughly 94% base rate for normal play and only go well below it if there is concrete evidence, such as a reported injury, a withdrawal or a mid-match retirement. Back-to-back events or a low market price are not enough on their own.

suggested_change.change: Block forecasts below 0.80 on tennis match-completion markets unless the research cites a specific injury, withdrawal or retirement report, and don't let a low market price pull the forecast toward it when no such report exists.

recent.question: Adana: Completed Match: Lucia Bronzetti vs Lois Boisson
recent.what_happened: Boisson, who got in as a lucky loser, beat 8th seed Bronzetti 6-1, 6-2 on September 29, 2026. The match was played to the end with no retirement, so the market resolved YES.
recent.what_we_missed: Most WTA matches finish normally, well over 90% of the time. Boisson had just played two full qualifying matches in Adana and had also played the US Open. Her one retirement in Philadelphia in August was not enough to justify a forecast of about 49% that the match would be completed. Our forecast was also below the market price of 0.545, which already looked too low.
recent.lesson: For 'completed match' questions, start from a base rate of roughly 93–97% and only go far below it if there is strong current evidence of injury, such as a withdrawal or retirement in the past few days, not an old one.

suggested_change.change: Put a floor of about 85% on forecasts for 'completed match' questions unless the research turns up a specific injury or retirement from the past week involving either player.

recent.question: Jingshan: Completed Match: Kristina Mladenovic vs Sofia Costoulas
recent.what_happened: The first-round match at the WTA 125 Jingshan was played on September 29 local time and finished through normal play, so the market resolved Yes. Search results show Mladenovic winning, although the exact score reported was garbled.
recent.what_we_missed: Our research-backed forecast of 0.36 leaned heavily on a few past retirements (Mladenovic in Les Sables d'Olonne and Lugano, Costoulas in Istanbul). That ignored the base rate: well over 90% of WTA matches finish normally. Both players had also just played a full doubles match in Singapore the week before, which suggested they were fit to play.
recent.lesson: Start from the base rate that about 93–97% of WTA matches are completed. Only move far below it on specific, current evidence of injury or withdrawal, not on a player's occasional past retirements.

suggested_change.change: When a 'completed match' forecast sits more than 30 points below both the base rate and the market price (0.90 here) without direct news of injury or withdrawal, cap how far it can move or flag it for review.

recent.question: Will France win on 2026-09-28?
recent.what_happened: France beat Belgium 1-0 in Brussels without Mbappé. Michael Olise scored the only goal in the 89th minute with a solo run and a low shot, so for 88 minutes the game was heading for a draw that would have resolved No.
recent.what_we_missed: Nothing important. The research-backed 0.47 was close to the market's 0.515, and the result came down to one late goal in a tight game. The no-research 0.36 gave too much weight to Mbappé's absence and Belgium's home unbeaten run, and too little to France winning 5 of the last 6 meetings and 8 of their last 9 away games.
recent.lesson: When a coin-flip away game ends on a single late goal, don't treat it as a forecasting error. Do note that one missing star, even Mbappé, moved France's win chance by only a few points, not ten or more.

suggested_change.change: Keep the current process. The forecast with research was well calibrated, and the only fix is to limit how much a single absent star moves forecasts made without research.

recent_wins.question: 1st inning: Over 0.5 runs
recent_wins.what_happened: In the top of the 1st, Kyle Schwarber drew a one-out walk against Chris Sale, and Alec Bohm drove him in with a two-out, 2-2-count double, so the Phillies led 1-0. That made the question resolve YES. Luzardo then threw a scoreless 10-pitch bottom of the 1st.
recent_wins.what_worked: Not much specific reasoning carried it. Our 0.56 was above both the league base rate the forecaster had (about 45% of games have a first-inning run) and the market's 0.415, even though two aces were pitching (Sale had a 2.16 ERA, and Luzardo's last start against Atlanta was a shutout). The only run came from a walk plus a two-out double with two strikes, which is close to a coin flip.
recent_wins.lesson: If a playoff game has an ace on each side and our number is above both the league base rate and the market, that needs a specific reason. A YES result doesn't show the edge was real.

suggested_change.change: When the forecast moves from the base rate toward the side that the pitching facts argue against, cut the bet size or require a written reason before betting on first-inning run markets.

recent_wins.question: Will there be more than 30 transit calls through the Strait of Hormuz from Sep 21, 2026 to Sep 27, 2026? (Above 30)
recent_wins.what_happened: The market resolved NO: IMF PortWatch counted 30 or fewer transit calls through Hormuz for Sep 21–27, 2026. Throughput stayed near 1% of normal after Trump rejected Iran's reopening proposal on Sep 27. PortWatch's Sep 21–27 daily figures were still unpublished in the sources I checked on Sep 29, so I couldn't confirm the exact total. Other trackers reported higher counts because they include dark (AIS-off) transits, e.g. Windward's 24 vessels on Sep 27 and 55 transits over Sep 16–23.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research anchored on PortWatch's own recent numbers: 78 transits over Sep 1–20 (about 27 a week), 8 on Sep 13 and 1 on Sep 20. It also noted that PortWatch is AIS-based and misses dark transits, so it discounted the higher Windward, Reuters and US-official counts. That moved the forecast from 42% without research to 15%, below the market's 20.5%.
recent_wins.lesson: When a question resolves on a specific data source, forecast from that source's recent run rate and how it counts. Treat other trackers' higher figures as noise unless they use the same method, here AIS-visible transits only.

suggested_change.change: For count questions tied to one data provider, always pull that provider's trailing 2–4 week totals and write down its counting rules, such as AIS-only, before looking at other sources.

recent_wins.question: Will Sweden win on 2026-09-28?
recent_wins.what_happened: Sweden beat Poland 3-1 at Strawberry Arena on 28 September 2026. Nygren scored in the 8th minute, Szymański equalised in the 43rd, and Ayari (63') and Gyökeres (72') won it for Sweden, who now have two wins from two in Nations League B Group 4. Sweden won within 90 minutes, so the market resolved YES.
recent_wins.what_worked: The research took the forecast from 0.35 to 0.55, about 10 points above the market's 0.445. The main reasons were Sweden playing at home, their 5-2 head-to-head record including a 3-2 win at the same ground in March, Poland failing to score against Bosnia, and Poland losing Kaminski. Even so, 55% is close to a coin flip on a result that had three possible outcomes, and Sweden were missing Isak, Holm and Ekdal. The evidence leaned the right way, but the outcome itself was largely luck.
recent_wins.lesson: When a home side has a clear head-to-head record against the same opponent, recent wins at the same venue and better current form, and its opponent is struggling to score, give those facts a few points of weight over the market even if the home side has headline injuries. Their depth may cover the missing players.

suggested_change.change: Before discounting a team for injuries, check who replaces the injured players and whether the team has won without them before (here Nygren, Ayari and Gyökeres covered for Isak), rather than treating a star's absence as a large penalty by default.

recent_wins.question: Will Türkiye win on 2026-09-28?
recent_wins.what_happened: Italy won 4-1 in Bursa on 2026-09-28. Bastoni, Frattesi and Kayode had them 3-0 up by the 27th minute. Barış Alper Yılmaz scored for Türkiye in the 47th, and Pio Esposito made it 4-1 in the 50th. So the market resolved No. Sources: [ESPN](https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/401861077), [Daily Sabah](https://www.dailysabah.com/sports/football/turkiye-concedes-4-1-to-italy-in-nations-league-match-in-bursa), [Goal](https://www.goal.com/en/lists/italy-turkiye-4-1-nations-league/bltf5040e172cf8be42), [beIN](https://www.beinsports.com/en-mena/football/uefa-nations-league/articles-video/italy-
recent_wins.what_worked: The forecast leaned on Türkiye never having beaten Italy in 16 meetings, and on Türkiye missing key players: Çakır suspended, Çalhanoğlu and Yıldız injured, Kökçü out with a toe injury. Both points held up. But a win-only market at 35.5% already made No the favourite, and 8% was much more confident than those facts justify. The unconfirmed '0-0 draw' search snippet was also wrong. The direction was right, but the size of the edge was partly luck.
recent_wins.lesson: A long winless head-to-head record plus a depleted home side is a real signal to shade below the market. Before going far below it, say how much of the gap comes from the evidence, and ignore unverified result snippets found before kickoff.

suggested_change.change: If a forecast is more than 20 points away from the market price and the research includes an unconfirmed result claim from before the match was played, drop that claim and cap the gap at what the confirmed evidence supports.

recent_wins.question: Will the price of Bitcoin be above $84,000 on September 28?
recent_wins.what_happened: BTC fell on Sep 28 as the dollar strengthened, bond yields rose and oil climbed after Trump rejected Iran's 7-day plan. It was about $82,958 at 7:20am ET and about $83,069 at 11:35am ET, so the noon Binance candle almost certainly closed below $84,000 and the market resolved NO.
recent_wins.what_worked: Very little, honestly. Our 0.46 was the most bullish number in the room, above jev_alone (0.37), claude_direct (0.32) and the market (0.245). A bold bet sized against a 0.245 price would have been on YES and lost. The research did find the key fact: at judgment time BTC was already about $83,300–83,600, below the strike, after a morning drop. But the forecast leaned on the week's closes near $84.4k instead of the live price and the macro headwinds (10-year yield above 5%).
recent_wins.lesson: For short-horizon price-threshold questions, anchor on the latest timestamped spot price and the distance to the strike in units of typical volatility over the remaining hours, not on the prior week's closes. When the market sits well below 0.5 and spot is already under the strike, explain why the market is wrong before disagreeing with it.

suggested_change.change: Block or shrink bets when the forecast is more than 15 points from the market on a crypto price question with less than 12 hours to resolution, unless the research includes a timestamped spot price that supports the gap.

rules.rule: For short-window crypto price questions, record a spot price from the exchange and pair named in the resolution rules (e.g. Binance BTC/USDT), taken as close to judgment time as possible, and state its timestamp and age.

For crypto threshold questions, report the percent distance from current spot to the strike, the hours left in the window, and recent realized volatility over a similar span, noting whether the window falls on a usually quieter weekend.

Read the resolution rules to see whether a crypto question needs any touch of the level during the window or a close at a specific candle and time, and measure the current price against that exact test.

Do not treat earlier-week touches of a level or prior days' closes as evidence about the current window; identify what drove those moves (e.g. a weekday bond-yield spike) and check whether that driver is still active now.

For short-horizon crypto questions, search same-day macro and geopolitical news (dollar, bond yields, oil, major policy statements) and report any specific catalyst with timestamps, or state plainly that none was found.
For single-match win questions, read the resolution rules to confirm whether only a win in regulation time counts, and state plainly that a draw would resolve No.

For match questions, report the full head-to-head record between the two teams and each side's confirmed suspensions and injuries, citing dated team, federation or reputable news sources for each absence.
Discard any search snippet claiming a match result that is undated or dated before kickoff; report a result only from sources published after the match was played.

retro.headline: Main strategy is up $3,378 on 2 of 2 winning bets, but only 18 markets have resolved, so nothing is established yet; the market price is still our best forecaster overall.
went_well: Main (Jev + Claude research) won both settled bets and is up $3,377.58. Two bets is luck-sized, not proof.
Claude direct scored a Brier of 0.097 against the market's 0.112, but it was judged on only 8 markets, possibly not the same ones.
Jev + research scored a Brier of 0.119 on 10 markets, far better than Jev alone at 0.336 on 18, so the research step looks like it matters.
went_badly: We are not beating the market: it scored 0.112 on all 18 resolved markets, and Jev + research (0.119, n=10) did not clearly beat it. In crypto (6 markets) the market scored 0.055 against research's 0.130.
Jev alone scored a Brier of 0.336 on 18 markets. That is worse than answering 50% every time (0.25), and it was worst in sports at 0.408 (n=9).

Of this week's reviewed outcomes, 2 misses were overconfidence and 2 of the 3 wins were judged lucky. The bold strategy is 1 for 3 with 25 bets still open, and the self-calibrating strategy can't start until 30 resolved markets exist (it has 10).
